question: For $k>0$, use the first derivative test to classify the critical points of $f(x)=x^3-3kx$. Obtain the corresponding local maximum and minimum values in terms of $k$.
explanation:
Critical points
$$f'(x)=3x^2-3k=3(x-\sqrt{k})(x+\sqrt{k})$$
Thus, the critical points are $x=-\sqrt{k}$ and $x=\sqrt{k}$.
Derivative sign
For $x<-\sqrt{k}$, $f'(x)>0$. For $-\sqrt{k}\sqrt{k}$, $f'(x)>0$.
Classification
At $x=-\sqrt{k}$, the derivative changes from positive to negative, giving a local maximum. At $x=\sqrt{k}$, it changes from negative to positive, giving a local minimum.
Extreme values
$$f(-\sqrt{k})=2k\sqrt{k}$$
$$f(\sqrt{k})=-2k\sqrt{k}$$
Conclusion
The local maximum is $2k\sqrt{k}$, and the local minimum is $-2k\sqrt{k}$.

options.A: Local maximum at $x=-\sqrt{k}$ with value $2k\sqrt{k}$; local minimum at $x=\sqrt{k}$ with value $-2k\sqrt{k}$
options.B: Local minimum at $x=-\sqrt{k}$ with value $2k\sqrt{k}$; local maximum at $x=\sqrt{k}$ with value $-2k\sqrt{k}$
options.C: Local maximum at $x=\sqrt{k}$ with value $2k\sqrt{k}$; local minimum at $x=-\sqrt{k}$ with value $-2k\sqrt{k}$
options.D: Both $x=\pm\sqrt{k}$ are local minima with value $-2k\sqrt{k}$
